items.title: Glenn Close receives honorary Oscar after eight nominations without a win
items.why: Actor Glenn Close received an honorary Oscar at the Academy's Governors Awards in Los Angeles on Sunday, her first Oscar after eight nominations. Director Ridley Scott and Disney animator Floyd Norman, 91, also received honorary Oscars.
items.matters: Honorary Oscars recognise whole careers; Close had been nominated eight times since 1983 without winning one.

items.title: China's factory output and shop sales slow more than expected
items.why: China's statistics bureau said on Monday that retail sales grew just 0.4% in October from a year earlier, down from 1.1% in September, despite a week-long national holiday. Industrial output rose 4.8%, below forecasts of 5.3%, and investment fell 8.1% over ten months.
items.matters: Weak spending in the world's second-largest economy affects demand for goods and commodities everywhere.

items.title: US and nine partners sign declaration to protect AI supply chains
items.why: The US State Department says ten countries, including India, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Israel, Qatar, the UAE, Singapore and the UK, signed the 'San Francisco Declaration' on 15 November. It sets up working groups on chips, minerals, energy and AI security. It is not a trade deal.
items.matters: Governments are grouping together to control who makes the chips and parts that AI depends on.

items.title: Japan's economy shrinks slightly as high oil prices hit spending
items.why: Japan's economy contracted at an annualised 0.1% in July to September, government figures showed on Monday, when economists had expected growth. Household spending fell as food and energy prices rose; Japan imports almost all its oil, and the yen is near 160 to the dollar.
items.matters: It shows how the Middle East war's oil shock is squeezing households even in rich economies.

items.title: Cape Verde's President Neves wins second term, provisional results show
items.why: José Maria Neves won about 63.8% of Sunday's presidential vote in Cape Verde, off West Africa, provisional results show. Joana Rosa, a former justice minister and the first woman to run for president there, took 31.6% and conceded. Only about a third of voters took part.
items.matters: Official results from the electoral commission are expected this week.

items.title: Pope Leo demands justice for murdered defenders of Peru's Amazon
items.why: Pope Leo XIV, on the second-to-last day of his South America tour, told Indigenous people in Pucallpa, in Peru's Amazon, that the blood of murdered forest defenders "demands justice". Campaign groups estimate 57 environmental defenders were killed in Peru between 2010 and 2024.
items.matters: He also warned at Mass against an "insatiable thirst for domination", linking the region's poverty to threats to its forests.

items.title: England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid, ending 43-match unbeaten run
items.why: England won 3-2 away to world champions Spain in the UEFA Nations League in Madrid on Sunday, despite playing the last half-hour with ten men. Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored. The result ended Spain's 43-match unbeaten run and put England top of their group.

items.title: Vulcan rocket fails, losing 40 Amazon internet satellites
items.why: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Sunday but failed to reach orbit after a problem about 10 minutes into flight. All 40 Amazon Leo satellites on board were lost. It is ULA's first outright failure since the company was formed in 2006.
items.matters: It sets back Amazon's plan for worldwide satellite internet, as Amazon must wait for the investigation before flying Vulcan again.

items.title: Estonia to close all border crossings with Russia from 1 December
items.why: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday Estonia will shut its three crossings after a foiled arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems near Tallinn on Saturday. Estonia says Russia's GRU military intelligence ordered it; eight suspects were detained. Moscow said the plan, if confirmed, would be "Russophobia".
items.matters: Estonia, a NATO and EU member, says closing the border will curb Russian hostile activity and sanctions evasion.

items.title: Ronaldinho, 46, plays his first competitive match in 11 years
items.why: Brazilian football star Ronaldinho, 46, played the first half for Italian third-tier club Ravenna in a 2-0 derby win over Forlì on Sunday, his first competitive match since 2015. Nearly 7,000 fans watched. Asked if he would play again, he said it was up to the club's president.

items.title: ASEAN and China miss deadline for South China Sea code of conduct
items.why: Talks on rules for the disputed South China Sea did not conclude at the ASEAN summit in Manila, the Philippines said on Sunday. Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro said about 80% of the draft is agreed; whether it will be legally binding is unresolved. Singapore, next year's chair, takes over.
items.matters: About half the world's merchant ships pass through the sea, where China and the Philippines have clashed repeatedly since 2022.

items.title: Rory McIlroy equals record with eighth Race to Dubai title
items.why: England's Tyrrell Hatton won the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, on Sunday by five shots. Runner-up Rory McIlroy overtook Spain's Eugenio Chacarra on the final day to win the season-long Race to Dubai for the eighth time, equalling Colin Montgomerie's record.

items.title: Indonesia's president apologises to Malaysia and Singapore over wildfire haze
items.why: Speaking at the ASEAN summit in Manila on 15 November, President Prabowo Subianto apologised for smoke from nearly four months of fires on Sumatra, Borneo and Papua. He said 17 company concessions had been revoked and that 16 firefighters had died fighting the blazes.
items.matters: Smoke from Indonesia's forest and peatland fires regularly harms air quality and health across Southeast Asia.

items.title: Yemen government forces pull back from Bab el-Mandeb, leaving Houthis in control
items.why: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces said on Sunday they were withdrawing from the area around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, at the mouth of the Red Sea, to defend their base in Aden. Reuters says it ends a six-week counteroffensive. Saudi Arabia's coalition said it intercepted Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh.
items.matters: Analysts quoted by The New Arab say the retreat gives the Houthis more leverage over a key shipping chokepoint.

items.title: COP31 climate talks in Türkiye enter final week as ministers take over
items.why: Ministers at the UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, now tackle the hardest questions: money for poorer countries and moving away from fossil fuels. A first draft of the main decision is due early this week, and the talks are scheduled to end on 20 November.
items.matters: The deal will shape how fast countries cut emissions and how much help vulnerable nations get to adapt.

items.title: South-east Asian nations sign a regional digital trade pact
items.why: ASEAN economic ministers meeting in Manila, the Philippines, signed a Digital Economy Framework Agreement covering e-commerce, online payments and data flows across the ten-member bloc.
items.matters: Shared online trade rules could make cross-border shopping and payments across the region easier and safer.

items.title: Wu-Tang Clan and Phil Collins join the Rock Hall of Fame
items.why: The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inducted its 2026 class at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on Saturday. Wu-Tang Clan performed a medley and Phil Collins gave a tearful speech; Cuban singer Celia Cruz and Nigeria's Fela Kuti were honoured posthumously. Oasis, Sade and Iron Maiden stayed away.

items.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas Rafah commander as allies urge tents for Gaza
items.why: Israel's military and Hamas say Samir Abu Younis, commander of Hamas's Rafah brigade, was killed in a strike in al-Mawasi, southern Gaza, overnight into Sunday. Separately, the UK, Australia, Canada and Italy urged Israel to let in 150,000 tents they say are held at the border as winter begins.
items.matters: Gaza's health ministry says at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect.

items.title: SpaceX catches a returning Starship upper stage with its launch tower
items.why: SpaceX's tower at Starbase, Texas, caught the Starship upper stage with its mechanical arms on 14 November, about 22 hours and 14 orbits after launch. It is the first such catch. The Super Heavy booster was not caught and was destroyed over the Gulf of Mexico.
items.matters: Catching both stages would let the rocket fly again quickly; NASA plans to use Starship to land astronauts on the Moon.

items.title: Data of 22 million people stolen in attack on French postal firm
items.why: La Poste says hackers stole names and postal addresses of about 22 million people from Maileva, its business mailing subsidiary, in mid-September. Bank details were not affected, it says. Maileva has told France's data protection authority and a judicial investigation is under way.
items.matters: Leaked names and addresses are often used for scam letters, texts and calls, so people should be wary.

items.title: Italy fines Meta €805 million over Facebook access to phone photos
items.why: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta €805 million, saying a Facebook feature reached into Android users' photo galleries by default without specific consent. About 20 million Italians use Android. Meta says the fine is 'disproportionate' and it will appeal.
items.matters: It tests how far apps may go in reading the private photos stored on your phone.

items.title: Wales beat New Zealand's All Blacks for the first time since 1953
items.why: Wales beat New Zealand 35-28 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Saturday, scoring five tries to four in the Nations Championship. It was their first win over the All Blacks in 73 years and ended a run of 34 straight defeats against them.
items.matters: Wales were rank outsiders; New Zealand must now beat England at Twickenham to keep their hopes of reaching the final.

items.title: Philippines' Carmelle wins the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Bangkok
items.why: Carmelle Collado, 19, won the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Bangkok, Thailand, on Saturday with "Sobra-Sobra", sung in Tagalog and English. She scored 211 points from juries and viewers, ahead of hosts Thailand and Vietnam. Eleven countries took part.
items.matters: Eurovision's first Asian edition gives singers from smaller music markets a stage, with viewers voting from 183 countries and territories.

items.title: Japan beat Brazil 3-2 with stoppage-time winner in Singapore
items.why: Japan beat Brazil 3-2 in a friendly at Singapore's National Stadium on Saturday in front of 38,688 fans. Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scored the winner in stoppage time; Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were sent off after protesting. Brazil had knocked Japan out of the World Cup in June.

items.title: Xi, Trump and Putin to hold first three-way summit in China
items.why: The White House and the Kremlin say the three leaders will meet on Thursday 19 November in Shenzhen, China, during the APEC summit. The White House says Trump wants to discuss cutting nuclear arsenals and the Iran war; a US official said Ukraine will not be discussed.
items.matters: A senior US official told Al Jazeera they expect no agreement, calling it the start of a conversation.

items.title: Nigeria warns travellers with health conditions about high-altitude Addis Ababa
items.why: Nigeria's foreign ministry says 16 Nigerians died this year while transiting through Ethiopia's capital, Addis Ababa, deaths it links to the city's altitude of about 2,350 metres. It urged people with heart or lung conditions to seek medical advice before travelling via the city.
items.matters: Addis Ababa's airport is a major hub used by millions of passengers each year, many connecting across Africa.

items.title: US reportedly loses measles elimination status after 26 years
items.why: A Pan American Health Organization panel has concluded that measles has spread continuously in the United States for more than a year, KFF Health News and AP report. The US declared measles eliminated in 2000. More than 5,400 cases have been confirmed this year, the most since 1991.
items.matters: Regaining the status needs at least 12 months without sustained spread; a formal announcement is expected on 17 November.

items.title: Voyager 1 to become first spacecraft one light-day from Earth
items.why: NASA says Voyager 1, launched in 1977, will be one light-day from Earth, about 25.9 billion kilometres, on Wednesday 18 November at about 10:16 GMT. A command from Earth now takes a full day to reach it, and the reply another day.
items.matters: No other human-made object has travelled so far; its power supply is expected to run out within about a decade.

items.title: Heirs ask Sotheby's to halt $180m Van Gogh sale over Nazi-era claim
items.why: Heirs of German Jewish publisher Samuel Fischer say Van Gogh's "Chestnut Trees in Blossom", estimated at $180m, was sold under duress in 1936 and want it withdrawn from Sotheby's New York sale on Wednesday. Sotheby's says its research has not shown duress but it is talking to the family.
items.matters: The case tests how auction houses handle art that Jewish families sold while escaping Nazi persecution.

items.changed: Updated 15 Nov: Bahrain says it intercepted fresh Iranian attacks; Iran says it targeted a US radar.
items.title: Bahrain intercepts new Iranian attacks; Iran says it targeted US radar
items.why: Bahrain says its air defences destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks on Sunday 15 November, its first such interceptions since September. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say six drones targeted a US radar at Riffa air base. On Friday the US said it downed two Iranian drones aimed at Bahrain.
items.matters: Bahrain hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet; Iran also says two tankers hit mines near Hormuz, which Reuters could not verify.

items.changed: Updated 14 Nov: Europe picks its five negotiating countries; Zelensky says the US floated NATO membership for the Donbas.
items.title: Europe names five countries for Ukraine talks; Zelensky reports NATO-for-Donbas idea
items.why: EU leaders meeting in Dublin on Friday chose Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland to represent Europe at the next round of US-mediated talks. Zelensky says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would leave the Donbas in exchange for NATO membership; the US has not publicly confirmed it.
items.matters: Zelensky says Ukraine won't withdraw, but could put a deal to a referendum if given firm security guarantees and funding.
